title: The Fox and the Grapes

sentences.text: A fox was walking under a grapevine when he saw a heavy bunch of grapes.
The grapes hung high above him, round and purple in the sun.
He wanted them at once, so he bent his legs and jumped.
His paws swished through the air and missed the bunch.
He backed up and jumped a second time, then a third time.
Soon he was hot, dusty, and out of breath.
The fox sat down, lifted his nose, and said the grapes were sour anyway.
He walked off as if he did not care about them at all.
The grapes were still sweet. He had not tasted a single one.

questions.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

choices.text: A fox who pretends he does not want grapes he cannot reach
A fox who learns how to grow a grapevine
A vine that falls down during a windstorm
A fox who shares ripe grapes with friends

questions.explanation: The fox tries, gives up, and calls the grapes sour. He never tastes one. The big idea is that he pretends not to want something he cannot have.

questions.prompt: The fox says the grapes are sour. What does sour mean here?

choices.text: Soft, warm, and ready to share

questions.explanation: Sour describes a sharp taste, like a lemon. The fox uses that word for the grapes. The last lines also say the grapes were still sweet.

questions.prompt: Why does the fox say the grapes are sour?

choices.text: He bit one grape and disliked the taste
A friend told him to leave the vine
He wants to feel better about not getting them
The sun cooked every grape on the vine

questions.explanation: The story never says he tasted a grape. He calls them sour only after he cannot reach them. That clue shows he is covering up his disappointment.

attribution: A retelling of a public-domain fable by Aesop. The wording is original.
